name: Terraform remote state
auth: Terraform uses a host Access token. The backend organization is the terraformbackend repository key; permissions are checked server-side for workspaces and state. An expired token receives 401 even if state credentials were previously cached.
fresh_home: Use new TF_DATA_DIR, TF_CLI_CONFIG_FILE and project directory; independent working copies must use independent data directories to exercise server locking.
prerequisites: Local terraformbackend repository; the administrator chooses encryptStates.
HTTPS origin and existing Terraform configuration intended to use remote state.
Remote backend means remote state with local execution; no hosted runs are supplied.

configure.code:
umask 077
AW_WORK=$(mktemp -d)
export AW_URL AW_REPO AW_TOKEN
export TF_CLI_CONFIG_FILE="$AW_WORK/terraform.rc"
export TF_DATA_DIR="$AW_WORK/data"
unset TF_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR
python3 - <<'PY'
import json, os
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import urlsplit
host = urlsplit(os.environ["AW_URL"]).netloc
Path(os.environ["TF_CLI_CONFIG_FILE"]).write_text("credentials " + json.dumps(host) + " {\n  token = " + json.dumps(os.environ["AW_TOKEN"]) + "\n}\n")
PY
configure.note: This writes runtime credentials to a mode-0600 file under AW_WORK. HTTPS discovery uses /.well-known/terraform.json; do not hard-code the service discovery response. Start in a new root directory with no existing .terraform directory.
backend.tf; replace authority with AW_URL without scheme and repository with AW_REPO. Terraform backend blocks do not interpolate environment variables.

publish.note: terraform apply writes the new state after its normal plan/approval flow. Run only for the intended infrastructure configuration.

steps.code:
terraform init -no-color
terraform plan -no-color
terraform apply

install.note: Read the server state using the authenticated backend.

limitations: This implements remote state and workspace locking with local execution, not Terraform Cloud remote plans/runs.
Backend migration and force-unlock are operational actions and are deliberately not part of connection setup.

contains: Terraform uses local execution with the remote state backend
a second Terraform working copy cannot plan while the first holds the lock
Terraform uses the kept backend token "expired-backend-token"
